triples.evidence: The elucidation of the structure of the double helix provided a hint as to how DNA divides and makes copies of itself.

triples.head: DNA
triples.evidence: The double-helix model suggests that the two strands of the double helix separate during replication, and each strand serves as a template from which the new complementary strand is copied.

triples.head: DNA strand

triples.head: Meselson and Stahl
triples.evidence: Meselson and Stahl were interested in understanding how DNA replicates. They grew E. coli for several generations in a medium containing a “heavy” isotope of nitrogen (15N), which gets incorporated into nitrogenous bases, and eventually into the DNA.
